conventions.convention: Each unordered interacting pair contributes once with energy −Jij ZiZj; the field term is −hi Zi. Free Hamiltonians include only internal supports, whereas conditional energies include every interaction support meeting the region.
The general interaction permits position-dependent bounded finite-range coefficients. Translation invariance and constant fields are additional hypotheses of the phase specializations.
Physical-time dynamics is conjugation by exp(itH/ℏ); the KMS strip has width βℏ, with lower boundary ω(Aαt(B)) and upper boundary ω(αt(B)A).
Specification composition satisfies γΛγΔ = γΛ for Δ ⊆ Λ. DLR measures are Borel probabilities fixed by every finite-region kernel; the empty-region kernel is the identity.
The correspondence concerns states on the full norm-completed quasi-local matrix algebra, including off-diagonal observables, under Countable Choice and the stated finite-matrix hypotheses.

Two-dimensional coexistence assumes uniform nearest-neighbor J > 0, zero field and βJ ≥ 2. This is sufficient only; neither criticality nor extremality is asserted. The pressure is dimensionless log-partition per site.

load_bearing.statement: For the inhomogeneous bounded finite-range diagonal spin-1/2 Ising interaction, β > 0, ℏ > 0, Countable Choice and the stated finite-matrix C*-identity, μ ↦ ωμ, defined locally by integrating diagonal matrix coefficients, extends uniquely to an affine bijection between Borel DLR measures and β-KMS states on the full quasi-local matrix algebra.

Under Countable Choice and the finite-matrix C*-identity, for local A in AX the finite self-adjoint matrix KX = ΣS:S∩X≠∅ Φ(S) gives αt(A) = exp(itKX/ℏ) A exp(−itKX/ℏ). Every local diagonal observable is fixed.

Under Countable Choice and the finite-matrix C*-identity, every β-KMS state with β > 0 for the diagonal Ising thermodynamic dynamics vanishes on every off-diagonal local product-basis matrix unit; every finite local density matrix is diagonal.

The bounded finite-range, possibly position-dependent Ising kernels are finite-range proper probability kernels satisfying γΛγΔ = γΛ whenever Δ ⊆ Λ. In the translation-invariant constant-field subcase they coincide with the specified CSM translated-shape kernels.

Under Countable Choice and the finite-matrix C*-identity, the two-dimensional diagonal nearest-neighbor Ising model with uniform J > 0, zero field, βJ ≥ 2 and ℏ > 0 has two distinct translation-invariant full-algebra β-KMS states with the stated opposite nonzero magnetization bounds. Its variable-field cubic pressure equals the classical pressure and has the stated separated secant bounds at zero.

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicitly assumed countable selection principle carried by quasi-local completion and cylinder-measure extension, and retained by the phase transfers.
Bijection proof step 4.1 extends equality of μωγΔ and μω from cylinder events to the generated Borel sigma-algebra.
Bijection proof step 4.2 establishes holomorphy of the uniformly convergent sequence of local-pair KMS strip functions.

concerns.concern: Assumption A1 says Countable Choice 'is used only in extending the consistent local cylinder probabilities to a Borel probability and in the CSM uniqueness inputs.' This theorem also inherits Countable Choice through its quasi-local completion supplier F12 and dynamics supplier F15, while no CSM uniqueness theorem is used in this correspondence proof. The Statement already assumes Countable Choice, so this is an inaccurate use-description rather than a missing hypothesis.

seams_checked.note: Compared the actual CSM specification, chain uniqueness, high-temperature uniqueness, coexistence, pressure-limit and pressure-cusp suppliers with their QSM uses. Pair normalization, translation-invariance hypotheses, strict influence bound, βJ ≥ 2 threshold, magnetization constant and secant directions are preserved. The inhomogeneous specification extension is proved locally.

The KMS definition, bounded-strip uniqueness and finite Gibbs characterization match the cited uses, including strip width βℏ, boundary order and finite-dimensional hypotheses. The full-algebra extension supplies both boundaries and uses uniform strip convergence.

The coexistence proof uses the translation automorphisms defined by product-basis relabeling to transfer stationarity. Its pressure identification is proved by finite diagonal trace equality and the CSM pressure supplier; it does not claim a general KMS/variational-equilibrium equivalence.

The physical phase-predictions consumer preserves all three specialized regimes, full-algebra scope, Countable Choice and finite-matrix assumptions. Substitution β = 1/(kBT) correctly gives T ≤ J/(2kB), retains the magnetization and pressure bounds, and makes no empirical, sharp-critical-temperature or extremality claim.
